title: Iran Lays Out Seven Conditions as Araghchi Works the Regional Phone Circuit
dek: Tehran says it will not discuss its nuclear proposal until Washington meets seven demands, as Iran's foreign minister calls regional counterparts.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The Strait of Hormuz, the waterway between Iran and Oman (file photo)

keyPoints: A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Iran sent a nuclear proposal to the US through Qatar, to be discussed only after Washington meets Tehran's seven demands, The National reported.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held separate calls with the foreign ministers of the UAE, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan on Thursday, The National reported.
Mohsen Rezaei, a senior Iranian security official, said during a visit to Russia that Iran has announced seven conditions to the Americans.
The US official quoted by Reuters said Washington was reviewing the proposal but gave no details.
body:
Iran has put seven conditions on any discussion of its nuclear proposal to the United States, a senior Iranian official told Reuters, as Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi spent Thursday on calls with regional governments.

## Seven conditions before talks

The Iranian official said Tehran sent a nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar. It would be discussed once the US met Iran's seven demands, the official said, according to Reuters as cited by The National. A US official told Reuters that Washington was reviewing the proposal and declined to give details. The seven demands were not itemized in the reporting reviewed for this story.

Mohsen Rezaei, a senior Iranian security official, said during a visit to Russia on Thursday: "On the issue of diplomacy, we have announced seven conditions to the Americans. As long as they do not execute our seven conditions..." The remarks as published by The National were cut off there, so this story does not characterize the rest of his statement.

## Regional calls

Araghchi held separate phone calls with the foreign ministers of the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, The National reported. The calls came as Qatari mediators held discussions with the White House and Tehran over a draft proposal.

## Context from Washington

President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he would decide soon whether to go further against Iran or pursue an agreement. Trump said: "I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible, but maybe I will have to. You'll know soon enough." Axios and Fox News reported that Trump met national security advisers on Wednesday and Thursday, and that US Central Command is finalizing preparations for a potential operation. No order to resume military operations had been issued, Fox reported.

See the companion story on Trump's options for the full context of the post-midterm decision.

## What we do not know

Reporting reviewed for this story does not say whether the US will accept any of Iran's seven conditions, or whether the draft proposal would be signed. It also does not give a date for talks.
